posts.linkedin:
Cups. Gloves. Labels.

Ordinary supplies can take a surprising amount of attention.

I'm building BUY HARD to make that everyday buying work easier: tell your buyer what's on hand, review a prepared purchase, and keep track of what arrives.

The new experience centers on a simple conversation and a clear next step. You approve spending.

We're inviting businesses to explore an early pilot. Bring one item you regularly reorder to a 20-minute walkthrough and we'll see how BUY HARD could help.

Explore the sample demo or book a walkthrough:
https://buyhard.app/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=buyhard_allgas_202609&utm_content=p1_intro

Built with Convex, OpenAI, Firecrawl, and AgentMail for the Convex All Gas Hackathon.

The public demo uses sample data.

"We have 8 cases of cups left."

That's how I want a stock update to start.

In BUY HARD, OpenAI helps the buyer understand everyday requests and prepare the work behind them. The conversation stays beside the inventory and buying tasks, so you can keep your attention on the business.

The goal is simple: say what changed, see the next step, and stay in control of purchases.

Try the sample conversation:

posts.linkedin:
Already have a product link? Start there.

One of the easiest ways to make buying software feel like work is to ask someone to type in details they already have.

BUY HARD uses Firecrawl to read product pages and bring item details into the buying process for review. A familiar supplier link becomes a starting point.

You review the information before using it. Reading a product page doesn't mean an order has been placed.

Bring one product link to a 20-minute walkthrough and we'll explore how BUY HARD could fit your business:
https://buyhard.app/walkthrough?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=buyhard_allgas_202609&utm_content=p3_firecrawl

Built with Convex, OpenAI, Firecrawl, and AgentMail for the Convex All Gas Hackathon.

The visual illustrates the workflow; it is not a supplier website or a completed order.
